Machuca retains small adobe houses built with straw and cactus wood. Visitors stop in the village after an early-morning trip to the El Tatio geysers.

During the stop, travelers discover local handicrafts and cuisine. This part of the itinerary complements the geothermal and high-altitude scenery with a glimpse of life in a small village.

Madidi National Park features on itineraries through the Bolivian Amazon. From the San Miguel del Bala area, travelers set off by boat along the Beni River and then continue on the Tuichi. Birds and rainforest mammals can be spotted along the banks.

Within the park, Caquihuara Ecolodge serves as the starting point for walking routes of varying difficulty. Guided walks with local experts offer a closer look at plants and animals in their natural habitat.

A short nighttime outing reveals another side of the forest: after sunset its sounds change, and many animals become more active.

The museum's collections place Peruvian art in historical context, from pre-Columbian traditions to later artistic movements. Specific exhibitions and access to galleries depend on the museum's current program.

The Exhibition Palace is recognizable by its long façade, arcades and park setting. On tours of Lima, MALI may be a dedicated stop or an agreed replacement for another museum or landmark. Visiting arrangements should be checked against the selected tour.

## Managua — Nicaragua's Capital!

Managua is Nicaragua's capital and largest city. It stands on the shore of the lake of the same name, also known as Lake Xolotlán, with the dormant Momotombo volcano rising across the water. Due to the active volcano, very few old buildings remain in Managua.

## Managua for Active Travelers!

Managua's central square is Revolution Square (formerly Republic Square), right beside the lake, and can be considered the city's historic center. Here stand Santiago Cathedral (the Old Cathedral), the National Theater and the National Palace of Culture. The nearby Central Park contains numerous monuments to national heroes. Opposite lies Rubén Darío Park, with a monument to Nicaragua's great poet carved from Carrara marble, regarded as the country's most monumental memorial. Managua is also popular with gambling enthusiasts, with four major casinos. Its favorable position between León and Granada has made Managua a significant trading center.
